stories.title: DPSCD continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results

Eighth graders saw a 7.6 percentage point increase in English proficiency, and seventh graders improved by 6.8 percentage points in math. SAT results also increased, with 35.1% of students meeting English benchmarks and 15.7% in math, up 6.6 and 4.3 percentage points respectively since 2019. stories.title: The Detroit school district continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed continued long-term improvement across all subjects in the 2026 M-STEP results, with significant gains in 8th grade English and 7th grade math compared to 2019. While year-over-year growth in early literacy was smaller and 6th grade proficiency dipped slightly, the district's 7th grade cohort outperformed peers. stories.title: Wayne-Westland Extends Intra-County Schools of Choice Application Deadline to September 25, 2026
stories.summary: Wayne-Westland Community Schools has extended the Intra-County Schools of Choice application window for non-resident students until September 25, 2026. Applications must include a two-year behavior report, attendance record, and recent academic records. Families are responsible for transportation if accepted.

stories.title: WCC earns community impact honors
stories.summary: WCC has received multiple honors and awards from state and local leaders, including the Environmental Excellence Partnership Program Award, Distinguished Service Award, and a tribute from Governor Gretchen Whitmer. State Rep. Jason Morgan also presented the college with a tribute for its high completion rate and Michigan Reconnect graduate numbers. President Bellanca emphasized the college's commitment to student success and community well-being.

stories.title: WCC Muslim Student Association builds community through Ramadan event
stories.summary: The Muslim Student Association at WCC hosted a Ramadan Annual Iftar event to bring students together through faith and education. The event aimed to foster community connections, challenge misconceptions about Ramadan, and highlight the significance of the holy month through guest speakers and interfaith collaboration.

stories.title: Weddings continue at new site as family rebuilds after historic barn fire
stories.summary: Historic Blum Barn, a wedding venue in Bridgewater Township, continues hosting weddings after a January fire destroyed its main barn. Despite most booked couples canceling, at least one bride kept her reservation, making the first wedding in the replacement space especially emotional for the family.

stories.title: Week of events celebrating Ann Arbor tech to return in September
stories.summary: Registration is now open for Ann Arbor SPARK’s a2Tech360, an annual weeklong series of events spotlighting Ann Arbor’s tech sector, which will return Sept. 22-Oct. 2. The event is organized by Ann Arbor SPARK and aims to highlight the region’s technology innovations and industry growth.

photo.alt: Ann Arbor SPARK board chair Kelly Sexton speaks at SPARK's annual meeting.

stories.summary: Student ambassadors at Schoolcraft College play a key role in welcoming new students. Their blue and gold polos make them easily identifiable, and they assist with campus events and orientations.

stories.title: What could winter be like in Michigan? Early predictions from Almanac
stories.summary: The Old Farmer's Almanac explains how the polar vortex and Quasi-Biennial Oscillation (QBO) influence winter forecasts for Michigan. Weakening of the polar vortex can bring colder Arctic air southward, leading to extreme winter weather outbreaks in the region.

stories.title: What will fall be like in Michigan? AccuWeather, NWS say warm and dry
stories.summary: Michigan's fall weather forecast for 2026 predicts warm and dry conditions, influenced by a potent El Niño event. NOAA's Michelle L'Heureux notes the El Niño duration is typical, with no atypical starting season or potential length. The forecast aligns with reports from AccuWeather and the National Weather Service.

stories.title: When do leaves change colors in Michigan? Where leaves are turning now
stories.summary: Here's when leaves began or will begin showing color across Michigan in 2026, according to Explore Fall's Michigan Fall Foliage Map: Western Upper Peninsula on Sept. 16, Eastern Upper Peninsula on Sept. 22, Northern Lower Peninsula on Sept. 28, and Southern Lower Peninsula on Oct. 2.

stories.title: When does daylight saving time end in 2026?
stories.summary: Unless Congress acts, daylight saving time is scheduled to end at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. The shift provides an extra hour of sleep but results in earlier sunsets during winter. The change is unlikely to affect Halloween, as it occurs after the holiday on Oct. 31.

stories.title: When does fall start in 2026?
stories.summary: The article explains that astronomical fall begins with the fall equinox on Sept. 22 at 8:04 p.m., while meteorological fall started on Sept. 1.

stories.title: When is Chipotle doing its free quesadilla promotion?
stories.summary: Chipotle is offering free quesadillas on Sept. 24 and 25 in honor of National Quesadilla Day. Customers must make a $20 purchase online or via the app using code 'NQD2026' to qualify. V&V Supremo Foods is also running a cash giveaway with $120 coupons for 103 winners.

stories.title: When will Daylight Saving Time end in 2026?
stories.summary: Daylight Saving Time will end at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, with clocks set back one hour. President Trump has urged senators to pass the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make DST permanent, but the bill's Senate approval remains uncertain.

photo.alt: When will Daylight Saving Time end in 2026?

stories.title: When will DST begin in 2027?
stories.summary: We'll spring forward at 2 a.m. on March 14, 2027, with clocks to be set one hour forward, marking the return of DST for 2027. This will make sunrise and sunset one hour later.

photo.alt: Clocks being set forward for daylight saving time.

stories.title: When will fall colors peak in Michigan?
stories.summary: The article provides estimated peak fall foliage dates for different regions in Michigan, including the Western Upper Peninsula on Sept. 30, Eastern Upper Peninsula on Oct. 17, Northern Lower Peninsula on Oct. 20, and Southern Lower Peninsula on Oct. 29.

stories.title: When will leaves turn colors? See latest fall predictions
stories.summary: Michigan's Upper Peninsula is starting to see fall colors emerge, with foliage in the western U.P. already changing and spreading east and south. The state is expected to see widespread color changes by early October, with southern Lower Peninsula cities like Lansing and Detroit being the last to turn. Peak viewing times range from late September through early November, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac.

stories.title: Why are judicial races in Michigan separated by incumbency?
stories.summary: Michigan's judicial elections separate incumbent judges into their own ballot sections under a 1982 law lobbied for by sitting judges. This practice allows incumbents to avoid competing directly with challengers, a system critics argue insulates judges from political pressures while proponents claim it protects judicial independence. The law was championed by former state Rep. Virgil C. Smith, who defended it as necessary to shield judges from 'the predatory nature of the political system.'

photo.alt: Why are judicial races in Michigan separated by incumbency?

stories.title: Why daylight saving time is suddenly back in the spotlight
stories.summary: The debate has gained new attention after Trump publicly urged senators to approve the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent and eliminate the twice-yearly clock changes. The House approved the bill in July, but its fate in the Senate remains uncertain. With less than three months until clocks are set to 'fall back,' lawmakers are running short on time if they hope to change the system before Nov. 1.

photo.alt: Why daylight saving time is suddenly back in the spotlight

stories.title: Why does the U.P. have a volcanic ridge?
stories.summary: A podcast episode explaining the geological history of the Upper Peninsula's volcanic ridge.

photo.alt: A picture from Eagle Harbor in the Upper Peninsula. The large green ridge you see in the background is the Greenstone Flow, which forms the spine of both the Keweenaw Peninsula and Isle Royale. The 'fingers' of black rock you see extending into Lake Superior are also lava flows--though much smaller--that were the 'last gasps' of the Midcontinent Rift System.

stories.title: Why Mike Duggan dropped out of the Michigan governor's race
stories.summary: Independent candidate Mike Duggan has dropped out of the Michigan governor's race with less than six months until midterms. The MichMash episode explores factors behind his decision and reactions from Democrats and Republicans, noting the political climate made an independent victory unlikely despite his potential.

photo.alt: Why Mike Duggan dropped out of the Michigan governor's race

stories.title: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous
stories.summary: A Detroit tenants union is suing the 36th District Court, arguing that landlords should not be allowed to evict tenants or collect rent for properties without a certificate of compliance. Landlords warn this could destabilize Detroit's rental market, potentially leading to foreclosures and higher rents, while tenants hope it will force improvements in housing conditions.

photo.alt: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous

stories.title: Will clocks fall back on Nov. 1? Here's the latest
stories.summary: The countdown to the next clock change is on, but President Donald Trump wants it to be one of the last. Americans are still expected to turn their clocks back on Nov. 1 as daylight saving time ends, despite the House passing a bill for year-round DST. The Senate is in recess until Sept. 14, and key lawmakers doubt there are enough votes to pass the measure before the fall time change, leaving the clock change likely to proceed.

photo.alt: Portrait of Saman Shafiq

stories.title: Will this be the last time we 'fall back'? Trump pushes end to DST
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is advocating for a permanent end to Daylight Saving Time, but legislation to achieve this faces uncertainty in Congress. The Sunshine Protection Act of 2025 requires Senate approval and Trump's signature, but Senate leadership has questioned its viability. If the bill fails, DST will end on Nov. 1, 2026, at 2 a.m.

photo.alt: Daylight Saving Time clock change illustration

stories.title: Will you still turn clocks back on Nov. 1?
stories.summary: Trump has long supported ending the twice-yearly clock changes, calling the practice 'foolish, inconvenient' and costly. He argues for permanent daylight saving time, citing benefits like fewer traffic accidents and energy savings. The House approved the Sunshine Protection Act in July, but its Senate fate remains uncertain as lawmakers race to act before Nov. 1.

photo.alt: Will you still turn clocks back on Nov. 1?

stories.title: Wisconsin DNR orders Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work
stories.summary: Wisconsin’s DNR ordered Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work near Iron County after an Aug. 25 spill. The agency cited a pattern of noncompliance, including unauthorized wetland disturbance, and may pursue enforcement action. Enbridge claims it’s working on cleanup and the bypass simultaneously.

stories.title: Woman fatally stabbed in Downtown Detroit, suspect in custody

The suspect, a man in his 40s, was taken into custody after being tracked via surveillance cameras. stories.title: Woman sentenced for false bomb threat at Lansing’s public transit center
stories.summary: A woman was sentenced to three years of probation for making a false bomb threat to Lansing's Capitol Area Transit Authority. Nefateria Denise Ferguson, 32, called in the hoax at 8:10 a.m. on April 22, 2025, and later admitted it was a prank.
